record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Can the temperature dependence of d.c. resistivity in metallic manganites be understood in enough detail to determine whether non-Fermi-liquid transport is present?

evidence.quote: The temperature dependence of the d.c. resistivity of manganites has not been sufficiently analyzed Can non-Fermi-liquid behavior be shown to be present in metallic manganites, as it occurs in many other exotic metals?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of doped perovskite manganite compounds of the form R_{1-x}A_x MnO_3, where R is a trivalent rare-earth cation (e.g., La, Pr, Nd) and A is a divalent alkaline-earth cation (e.g., Ca, Sr, Ba), in the doping range and temperature regime where the bulk material is in a metallic phase (i.e., the d.c. resistivity ρ(T) decreases with decreasing temperature). In a conventional Fermi liquid one expects, at low temperatures, ρ(T) = ρ_0 + A T^2, where ρ_0 is the residual resistivity and the T^2 term arises from electron–electron scattering. A non-Fermi-liquid metal is, by contrast, characterized by an anomalous power-law or other non-analytic low-temperature dependence, e.g., ρ(T) - ρ_0 ∝ T^α with α ≠ 2 (commonly α between 1 and 5/3) over a wide temperature window, signaling the breakdown of Landau quasiparticle transport.

Problem. Provide a sufficiently detailed quantitative analysis of the temperature dependence of the d.c. resistivity ρ(T) of metallic manganites — including the identification of the dominant scattering mechanisms (electron–phonon, electron–magnon, electron–electron, polaronic, spin-cluster, etc.), the functional form of ρ(T) over the accessible temperature range, and the low-temperature exponent α — to decide unambiguously whether the metallic phase of manganites exhibits non-Fermi-liquid transport, as observed in various other strongly correlated metals.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open-ended physics question about whether metallic manganites exhibit non-Fermi-liquid d.c. transport. The question was posed as an open issue in the early 2000s manganite literature, and while many subsequent experimental and theoretical studies have analyzed ρ(T) in metallic manganites (often fitting T^2 or T^{4.5} forms), no community-wide consensus identifying a definitive non-Fermi-liquid regime appears to have been established. Status is therefore taken as unknown/open.
